title: Unit – 3 : Session – 2 : SLO – 2 | Creating Threads with Runnable
sections: Fill: In Java, a class implements the RUNNABLE interface to create a thread using Runnable.
T/F: The run() method must be defined when implementing Runnable. — TRUE
MCQ: Correct way to create a thread using Runnable → A) new Thread(new MyRunnable()).start();
Fill: The Runnable interface belongs to the java.lang PACKAGE.
T/F: Runnable can be used to create multiple threads sharing the same task. — TRUE
MCQ: Keyword used when a class uses the Runnable interface → B) implements
Fill: The run() method of a Runnable object is invoked by the THREAD class.
T/F: Runnable allows better separation of thread creation and task definition. — TRUE
MCQ: Advantage of Runnable over extending Thread → B) Allows sharing the same task between threads
Fill: A thread is started by calling the START() method on the Thread object.
